newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia tenders to sell Hilton-managed hotel.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia tenders to sell Hilton-managed hotel.

text.p: Tuesday launched an international tender to sell a Hilton-managed hotel as part of its privatisation programme, official sources said.
Officials said buyers would be expected to modernise the
467-bed Hilton in Tunis, which is owned by the state tourism agency and which has been leased to London-based Hilton International since it was built in 1965.
Tourism sector sources said that South Korean group
Daewoo and Saudi investor Prince al-Waleed bin Talal had previously shown interest in buying the hotel. Both are expanding their business activity in North Africa.
Tunisia made massive investments in tourism in the 1960s
and 1970s in a successful bid to attract private investors.
The government has sold more than 20 hotels over the
last ten years as part of its privatisation programme. In the next few months, the government plasn to sell the Africa-Meridien hotel in Tunis.
